content.comment_body: I forgot the password on my [product_name]. Is there a universal password or another way to recover access? Thanks.

The password protection works as intended—there is no universal password or backdoor. The only option is to delete the program. Even though it asks for the password, if you attempt deletion three times, the program is eventually removed. Best regards, [user_name], Technical Support for Automation & Drives at [company_name].
There is an EEPROM inside. You could theoretically dump its contents and try to extract the password using a Hex editor, but I can't provide further details.
Thank you for your help, [user_name]! I had the same issue, followed your advice, and the program was cleared.
Does this approach also apply to the seventh generation? And is it possible to use a USB PC cable to dump the EEPROM?

For older [product_name] models with a display and buttons (up to [article_no], [version_no] 3), entering an incorrect password three times would clear the program and allow using the device for a new program. Reports about unauthorized deletions led [company_name] to modify this behavior from [article_no] [version_no] 4 onward. Now, you must use [product_name] V6.1 or a blank memory card, transferring the program by cycling the power. The process is still possible, but different now!

Hi Technical Support, what is the new FAQ number for this issue? The old method involved entering an incorrect password three times, but it's changed for [article_no] [version_no] 4. Is there a support note about this? Thanks.
I forgot the password on my [product_name] [article_no]. Is there a universal password? Thanks.
Did you review the previous posts in this thread?

analysis.insight_summary: Users forgetting their passwords on [product_name] devices up to and including [article_no] encounter strict protection with no universal or backdoor solution. In earlier models, the program would be erased after three failed attempts, allowing reuse, but from [article_no] [version_no] 4 onward this mechanism was changed due to abuse. Password resetting now requires more complex steps using [product_name] V6.1 or specific hardware methods, which increases legitimate recovery complexity while enhancing security against unauthorized access.
analysis.user_expectations: Users hope for a straightforward way to reset or recover a forgotten password, ideally without losing data, and are searching for an easy-to-use recovery method.
